opencode-gemini-sub

Use a Google Gemini subscription in OpenCode V2 — through the Antigravity or Gemini CLI client protocol.
Full tool calling, streaming, model discovery, a live quota sidebar and quota-aware auto-continue.

> [!WARNING] > **Unofficial and not affiliated with Google.** This plugin emulates Google's own clients > (Antigravity / Gemini CLI) to use their subscription entitlements from OpenCode. Google's > terms may treat this as a policy-violating use case and may restrict or terminate accounts. > Use it only with your own account, at your own risk, and read [`LEGAL.md`](LEGAL.md) first. > > Antigravity access depends on your plan and account. The Gemini CLI profile is rejected for > the individual tier (`UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT`); it remains useful for paid Code Assist > Standard/Enterprise subscriptions only. If you need the lowest-risk setup, use the official > Gemini API key or Vertex AI provider instead. > > **No warranty and no liability.** No guarantee is given for the information in > [`LEGAL.md`](LEGAL.md). To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no > liability for damages, data loss, account restrictions, suspensions, terminations, charges > or any other loss arising from the use of this software. Use at your own risk. ## Why OpenCode ships first-class support for ChatGPT and Copilot subscriptions, but not for Google's consumer plans. This plugin closes that gap without an API key: * the **Antigravity** profile speaks the current consumer protocol and gives you Gemini, Claude and GPT-OSS models from a Google AI Pro/Ultra plan; * the **Gemini CLI** profile speaks the Code Assist protocol for paid Standard/Enterprise organizations; * both keep OpenCode's native Gemini request format, so function calling, thought signatures and streaming work unchanged. ``` OpenCode ──Gemini REST──▶ loopback proxy ──Cloud Code Assist──▶ Google │ ├─ OAuth tokens (per profile) ├─ quota gate + auto-continue └─ model discovery ``` ## Features | Feature | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Zero-loss tool calling** | OpenCode's Gemini payload passes through untouched: `tools`, `parametersJsonSchema`, `functionCall`/`functionResponse`, `thoughtSignature` | | **Streaming** | Native SSE, unwrapped from the Code Assist envelope by an incremental parser | | **Thinking** | Requests ask for Gemini thought summaries (`includeThoughts`). Whether text arrives is up to the gateway; see [Thinking](#thinking) | | **Model discovery** | `fetchAvailableModels` for Antigravity; ids, names, context/output limits and image support come from your account | | **Two account limits** | 5-hour window and weekly limit per pool (`retrieveUserQuotaSummary`), not per-model noise | | **Auto-continue** | On quota errors the request stays open, the gate wakes at the reset timestamp, then the same request resumes | | **Sidebar** | Live usage panel: `5h`/`1w` for Antigravity, API usage for Gemini CLI | | **Quota tool** | Agents can inspect account, project, tier, limits and gate state with `gemini_quota` | | **Local-only credentials** | Tokens live in a `0600` JSON file; no telemetry, no analytics | ## Prerequisites - OpenCode **2.x** (`opencode --version`). - Node **22.18+** for the helper CLI (the plugin itself runs inside OpenCode's Bun runtime). - A Google account with Antigravity access, or a paid Code Assist Standard/Enterprise subscription for the Gemini CLI profile. ## OAuth client identity This repository ships **no Google credentials**. Login needs the installed-app OAuth client pair of the client whose entitlement you use. Provide it per profile via environment: ```bash export OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID="..." export OPENCODE_ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET="..." ``` or in the plugin options: ```jsonc "options": { "oauth": { "antigravity": { "clientId": "...", "clientSecret": "..." } } } ``` The Gemini CLI profile uses `OPENCODE_GEMINI_SUB_CLIENT_ID` / `OPENCODE_GEMINI_SUB_CLIENT_SECRET` (or `options.oauth["gemini-cli"]`). Without these values login fails with a clear message. Obtaining a compatible identity is your responsibility; see [`LEGAL.md`](LEGAL.md). ## Install Clone the repository somewhere stable: ```bash git clone https://github.com/officialPlocki/opencode-gemini-sub.git ~/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub-src cd ~/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub-src npm install --omit=dev ``` Add it to the **global** OpenCode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ { "package": "/home/you/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub-src", "options": { "profiles": ["antigravity"] } } ] } ``` Reload OpenCode (`/reload`), then run `/models` and pick an `antigravity/...` model. > [!NOTE] > OpenCode caches plugin modules by path. After updating the code, bump the version and > install into a versioned directory (`npm run install:local` does this) or restart the > service, otherwise the old module stays loaded. ## Sign in ```text /antigravity-login ``` A browser opens (the URL is also posted into the session). Use a browser on the same machine: the OAuth callback is a loopback port. Headless machines: ```bash node bin/gemini-sub.js login --profile antigravity ``` The CLI prints the URL and waits for the redirect. Credentials are shared with the plugin. Other commands: ```bash node bin/gemini-sub.js status --profile antigravity --quota node bin/gemini-sub.js quota --profile antigravity node bin/gemini-sub.js models --profile antigravity node bin/gemini-sub.js logout --profile antigravity ``` For the paid Code Assist profile use `--profile gemini-cli` and `/gemini-login`. ## Usage 1. Run `/models` and choose a model, e.g. `antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash-low`. 2. Work as usual. Tool calls, subagents and streaming are handled by OpenCode. 3. Open the sidebar to see the remaining 5-hour and weekly limits of the active pool: ```text GEMINI USAGE Gemini Models ▶ ready 5h ██████ 98% frei · 4h22 1w ██████ 100% frei · 6d23h ``` While a request is parked on a quota window: ```text ⏸ waiting 1m · 18:07 ``` The panel is visible whenever one of the plugin's models is selected — idle or running. It disappears when you switch to a model from another provider. ### Commands and tools | Command / tool | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `/antigravity-login` · `/antigravity-logout` | Sign in/out of the Antigravity profile | | `/gemini-login` · `/gemini-logout` | Same for the Gemini CLI profile (if enabled) | | `/gemini-status` | Accounts, projects, tiers, limits, gate state, unavailable models | | `/gemini-models` | Models exposed by each profile | | `/gemini-autocontinue on\|off` | Toggle waiting for a quota reset at runtime | | `gemini_quota` (tool) | Machine-readable status for agents | ## Auto-continue Enabled by default. On a quota or rate-limit error the proxy does **not** forward the 429: 1. classifies the error (Google RPC `RetryInfo`, `QuotaFailure`, `Retry-After`, prose hints); 2. resolves the reset from `retrieveUserQuotaSummary` (5h/weekly) or the error itself; 3. parks all in-flight requests on a shared gate until reset + a small buffer; 4. keeps the SSE connection alive with comment frames; 5. retries the identical envelope, so the agent loop and tool state survive. Terminal cases are reported immediately: spending caps, `limit: 0`, a reset beyond `maxQuotaWaitMs`, or an ineligible account. Runtime toggle (not persisted): ```text /gemini-autocontinue off /gemini-autocontinue on ``` Persistent default: ```jsonc { "options": { "autoContinue": false } } ``` ## Configuration ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "/home/you/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub-src", "options": { "profiles": ["antigravity"], "autoContinue": true, "maxQuotaWaitMs": 86400000, "keepAliveMs": 15000, "concurrency": 2, "antigravityVersion": "2.24.0", "models": [{ "id": "gemini-3-flash", "context": 1048576 }] } } ] } ``` | Option | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `profiles` | `["antigravity","gemini-cli"]` | Enabled connection profiles | | `autoContinue` | `true` | Wait for the quota reset instead of returning the 429 | | `maxQuotaWaitMs` | `86400000` (24 h) | Longest accepted wait; `0` = unlimited | | `keepAliveMs` | `15000` | SSE comment interval while parked | | `concurrency` | `2` | Max parallel upstream requests per profile | | `antigravityVersion` | `2.24.0` | Hub version reported in the User-Agent | | `antigravityUseLegacyHeaders` | `false` | Add older `X-Goog-Api-Client`/`Client-Metadata` headers | | `endpoint` | per profile | Override the backend host (tests/proxies) | | `projectId` | resolved | Force a Cloud project | | `models` | built-in + discovery | Add or override model metadata | | `dataDir` | `~/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub` | Credential directory | | `includeThoughts` | `true` | Ask Gemini models for thought summaries (Claude/GPT-OSS never get this field) | | `telemetry` | `false` | Send usage metrics like the original client | | `mock` | `false` | Canned responses, development only | | `debug` | `false` | Log proxy decisions | Client identity is configured through the environment variables or `oauth` options described in [OAuth client identity](#oauth-client-identity). No defaults are shipped. ## Models Antigravity models are discovered per account (`fetchAvailableModels`). Typical ids: ``` gemini-3.8-flash-high | -medium | -low | -tiered gemini-3.5-flash-lite | gemini-3.1-flash-lite | gemini-3-flash claude-sonnet-4-6 | claude-opus-4-6-thinking | gpt-oss-120b-medium ``` Interna (`chat_*`, `tab_*`), aliases (`gemini-2.5-*`), image and disabled entries are filtered. Availability is account-specific: Google serves different ids to different plans, and models such as `gemini-4-argon-disabled` stay hidden until the backend enables them. ## Thinking The plugin sets `generationConfig.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts = true` for Gemini models (never for Claude or GPT-OSS, which reject the field). Reviving the text in the transcript also needs the CLI setting: ```json title="~/.config/opencode/cli.json" { "session": { "thinking": "show", "tps": true } } ``` `session.tps` shows output tokens per second in assistant footers. **Gateway limitation:** for tool-enabled requests the Antigravity backend often returns a thought part with empty text — a signature carrier, not a summary. I verified this against the API: the same request without tools returns a readable summary, with tools the only thought part has `text: ""`. Some models (for example `gemini-3-flash` or `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) are more generous than the 3.8 Flash family, but no client-side change can create text the backend does not send. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause / fix | | --- | --- | | `Not signed in` | `/antigravity-login` | | `redirect_uri_mismatch` | Google rejected the loopback callback; check the exact error page | | `UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT` | Gemini CLI profile: Google disabled the individual tier; use Antigravity or a paid project | | `no Cloud project` after onboarding | Set `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` to a project with the Gemini for Google Cloud API enabled | | Model missing | Not in your account's inventory, or filtered as internal/disabled | | `maxQuotaWaitMs` error | Raise the limit or retry later | | Panel shows stale numbers | It refreshes via RPC every 2.5 s; `/gemini-status` forces a quota lookup | Server logs contain `[gemini-sub] ...` lines. Set `debug: true` for per-request decisions. ## Security & privacy - OAuth tokens are stored locally in `~/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub/*.json` with mode `0600`. - No analytics, no telemetry by default, no third-party servers. Requests go to Google only. - The loopback proxy binds `127.0.0.1` and uses a random secret path segment. - Treat the credential files like passwords. Revoke access from your Google account if in doubt. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for reporting and details. ## Disclaimer No warranty, guarantee or representation is made regarding the information in this repository (including `LEGAL.md`). It is general information for users, not legal advice, and may be incomplete or outdated. Obtain independent legal advice for your situation. To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the authors and contributors accept **no liability** for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, loss of data, loss of profits, business interruption, account restrictions, suspensions, terminations, billing charges or other losses arising from the use of or inability to use this software — even if advised of the possibility of such damages. You use it at your own risk and are solely responsible for compliance with Google's terms and applicable law.

# User information and risk notice

This page explains what this plugin does, what it needs from you, and what can happen when you
use it. It is written for people using the software, not as a legal memo, and it is **not legal
advice**. Google's terms and your local law always take precedence over anything written here.

## What this software does

`opencode-gemini-sub` connects OpenCode to Google's Cloud Code Assist backend by emulating the
network behaviour of two Google clients:

* the **Antigravity** client, for consumer Gemini/Claude/GPT-OSS access, and
* the **Gemini CLI / Code Assist** client, for organization-backed Code Assist.

It logs in with your Google account through OAuth and sends your prompts to Google. It does not
proxy your traffic through a third-party server. No Google source code is copied or bundled;
the protocol was reconstructed from observation.

## What you need

* Your **own** Google account. Do not use accounts you are not allowed to use.
* A compatible **OAuth client identity** (client id and secret). This repository ships none;
  you provide it through environment variables or plugin options. Obtaining a compatible
  identity is your responsibility.
* A plan that actually grants the entitlement you expect. Antigravity access is account- and
  plan-dependent. The Gemini CLI profile is rejected for the individual tier
  (`UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT`) and only makes sense for paid Code Assist subscriptions.

## What Google may do

Using an unofficial client is not something Google endorses. In practice this means:

* Google can change, restrict or block the endpoints or client identities at any time.
* Google can rate-limit, suspend or terminate accounts it associates with this kind of traffic.
* Requests can start failing after a client update, a policy change or a rollout.
* Your usage still counts against your plan's limits, and limits can change.

None of this is in the plugin's control, and none of it is a bug in the plugin.

## Your responsibility

* Comply with Google's terms, your plan's conditions and applicable law.
* Keep your credential files private (`~/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub/`, mode `0600`).
* Do not use the software to attack, scrape, resell or bypass limits for others.
* Accept that you use an unofficial client at your own risk.

# Security policy

## Supported versions

The current `0.2.x` line receives fixes. Older versions may break when Google changes the
protocol and are not supported.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report security issues privately:

* open a **private security advisory** on the repository (GitHub → Security → Advisories), or
* contact the maintainer through the repository's listed contact channel.

Do not open a public issue for credential leaks, auth bypasses or local privilege issues.
Include reproduction steps, affected version and, if relevant, a redacted log excerpt.

## Credential handling

* OAuth access and refresh tokens are stored as JSON under
  `~/.local/share/opencode-gemini-sub/` (or the configured `dataDir`), created with mode `0600`.
* The files are never uploaded by the plugin. There is no analytics or telemetry code path.
* The optional `telemetry` setting sends usage metrics to Google like the original client; it
  is off by default and never includes prompts or credentials.
* The loopback proxy listens on `127.0.0.1` with an ephemeral port and a random path segment.
  It is not reachable from other hosts.
* The helper CLI shares the same credential files. Run it only as the user who owns them.

## Revoking access

Sign out with `/antigravity-logout` (or `node bin/gemini-sub.js logout --profile antigravity`)
and revoke the application's access from your Google account security settings. Deleting the
credential file is enough on the local side.

## Scope

This plugin is an unofficial client. Reports about Google's service behaviour, quotas or
account eligibility are not vulnerabilities in this project.

# Reverse-engineered protocol notes

This document describes the Code Assist ("cloudcode-pa") backend as it is used by subscription-backed Gemini clients, and how `opencode-gemini-sub` maps OpenCode's Gemini REST traffic onto it.

## Clean-room statement

Everything here was derived from observable HTTP behaviour and from public documentation of Google RPC error types. No Google source file is copied, vendored, or transpiled. The implementation in `src/` is original.

Two literals must match the original client because the backend validates them:

* the public OAuth client id/secret pair of the installed Gemini CLI application (a public installed-app credential, not a cryptographic secret),
* the client metadata enum values (`pluginType: "GEMINI"`, …).

Both are configurable (`OPENCODE_GEMINI_SUB_CLIENT_ID`, `OPENCODE_GEMINI_SUB_CLIENT_SECRET`) and are protocol identifiers, not code.

## Endpoints

| Purpose | Method | URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tier/project negotiation | POST | `https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:loadCodeAssist` |
| First-time onboarding | POST | `…/v1internal:onboardUser` |
| Onboarding long-running operation | GET | `…/v1internal/<operationName>` |
| Streaming generation | POST | `…/v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` |
| Non-streaming generation | POST | `…/v1internal:generateContent` |
| Token counting | POST | `…/v1internal:countTokens` |
| Quota buckets | POST | `…/v1internal:retrieveUserQuota` |
| Admin controls | POST | `…/v1internal:fetchAdminControls` |
| Usage metrics (opt-in) | POST | `…/v1internal:recordCodeAssistMetrics` |

All calls are `POST` + JSON except operations, with `Authorization: Bearer <oauth access token>`.

## OAuth

* Authorization: `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`, response type `code`, PKCE `S256`, `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent`.
* Redirect: `http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>/oauth2callback` (installed-app loopback).
* Scopes: `cloud-platform`, `userinfo.email`, `userinfo.profile`.
* Token exchange/refresh: `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` with `grant_type=authorization_code|refresh_token`.
* Refresh tokens are long-lived; access tokens expire after ~1 h. The client refreshes 60 s early and on any `401`.

## Request envelope

OpenCode speaks the ordinary Gemini REST API:

```http
POST /v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-pro:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse
{ "contents": [...], "tools": [...], "systemInstruction": {...}, "generationConfig": {...} }
```

The proxy converts it to:

```jsonc
{
  "model": "gemini-2.5-pro",          // bare id, no "models/" prefix
  "project": "<cloudaicompanionProject>",
  "user_prompt_id": "<uuid>",
  "request": {
    "contents": [...],                 // unchanged, Gemini Content[]
    "systemInstruction": {...},        // unchanged
    "tools": [{ "functionDeclarations": [...] }],
    "toolConfig": {...},
    "generationConfig": {...},
    "safetySettings": [...],
    "session_id": "<stable per plugin instance>"
  }
}
```

`request` is a standard `GenerateContentRequest`; only `session_id` is added. Fields unknown to the backend are stripped before wrapping (transport-only keys such as a body-level `model`).

`loadCodeAssist` expects:

```jsonc
{
  "cloudaicompanionProject": "<optional project>",
  "metadata": { "ideType": "IDE_UNSPECIFIED", "platform": "PLATFORM_UNSPECIFIED", "pluginType": "GEMINI", "duetProject": "<project>" }
}
```

and returns `currentTier`, `paidTier`, `allowedTiers`, `cloudaicompanionProject`, `ineligibleTiers`. If no project is returned and a default tier exists, `onboardUser` is called and the returned operation is polled until `done`.

## Response format

Non-streaming:

```json
{ "response": { "candidates": [...], "usageMetadata": {...} }, "traceId": "..." }
```

Streaming (`text/event-stream`), one JSON object per event:

```text
data: {"response":{"candidates":[{"content":{"role":"model","parts":[{"text":"Hi"}]}}]},"traceId":"…"}
```

The proxy removes the outer `response` key and re-emits plain Gemini events, so OpenCode's Google provider sees exactly what it expects, including `functionCall`, `functionResponse`, `thoughtSignature` and `usageMetadata`.

## Errors and quota

Errors are Google RPC envelopes:

```jsonc
{
  "error": {
    "code": 429,
    "message": "…",
    "status": "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED",
    "details": [
      { "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.QuotaFailure", "violations": [{ "quotaId": "…PerDay…" }] },
      { "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.RetryInfo", "retryDelay": "3421s" },
      { "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo", "reason": "MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Classification used by `src/errors.ts`:

| Signal | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | refresh token, retry once |
| `403` + `VALIDATION_REQUIRED` | terminal, tells the user to finish Google's check |
| `RetryInfo.retryDelay`, `Retry-After`, "retry in Xs" | wait that long |
| `QuotaFailure` id containing `PerDay`/`Daily` | quota window; wait for `retrieveUserQuota` reset |
| long delay (> 10 min) | quota window |
| `ErrorInfo.reason` `MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED/EXCEEDED` | retry with backoff |
| "spending cap", "billing limit", `limit: 0` | terminal |
| bare `429` | retry after 60 s |

Quota reset resolution order:

1. timestamp in the error,
2. `RetryInfo`/`Retry-After`/prose delay,
3. `retrieveUserQuota` → earliest `resetTime` of exhausted buckets (fallback: any bucket),
4. 60 s fallback.

`retrieveUserQuota` returns:

```json
{ "buckets": [{ "modelId": "gemini-2.5-pro", "remainingFraction": 0, "resetTime": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }] }
```

## Client identity

Observed header shape:

```text
User-Agent: GeminiCLI/<version>/<model> (<platform>; <arch>; <surface>)
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The plugin emits the same shape with `{model}` substituted, overridable through options. No other fingerprinting tricks are used.

## What is intentionally not emulated

* `recordCodeAssistMetrics` is off by default (opt-in via `telemetry`). Sending telemetry is not required for the protocol to work.
* Embedding, image/video/speech generation and other non-chat surfaces are not proxied. The subscription entitlement for those is separate.
* Model discovery: the backend has no usable pre-conversation listing here, so the catalogue is local and configurable.

## Confidence and limits

The request/response shapes above are verified against the backend's documented Google RPC types and against real client traffic patterns. They are **not** verified against a live subscription in this repository's test suite, because that requires a personal Google account. The proxy, SSE translation, quota gate and error classification are covered by automated tests with a fake backend, and the whole path is exercised end-to-end in OpenCode's `mock` mode, including a real tool-call round trip.

# Antigravity profile

Google's Antigravity client uses the same Cloud Code Assist transport as the Gemini CLI, but with its own OAuth application, host, headers and envelope. The plugin implements it as a separate profile.

## OAuth

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Client id | supplied by the user (installed-app identity of the official client) |
| Callback | `http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>/oauth-callback` |
| Scopes | `cloud-platform`, `userinfo.email`, `userinfo.profile`, `cclog`, `experimentsandconfigs`, `openid` |

`cclog` and `experimentsandconfigs` are Antigravity-specific; without them the token is not accepted by the daily host.

## Host

`https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com` for every call (`loadCodeAssist`, `onboardUser`, `fetchAvailableModels`, `generateContent`, `streamGenerateContent`). Consumer entitlements are bound to this host; mixing it with the production host can produce mismatched tiers.

## Headers

Current Hub style (default):

```http
User-Agent: antigravity/hub/2.24.0 (aidev_client; os_type=linux; arch=x64; cl=1000335682)
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Older clients also send:

```http
X-Goog-Api-Client: google-cloud-sdk vscode_cloudshelleditor/0.1
Client-Metadata: {"ideType":"ANTIGRAVITY","platform":"PLATFORM_UNSPECIFIED","pluginType":"GEMINI"}
```

Set `antigravityUseLegacyHeaders: true` to add those. Onboarding calls append `google-api-nodejs-client/10.3.0` to the User-Agent and use `X-Goog-Api-Client: gl-node/22.21.1`, matching the Hub's control-plane requests.

The Hub version is configurable (`antigravityVersion`). Newer models are gated on a minimum Hub version, so keep it current.

## Envelope

```jsonc
{
  "project": "<cloudaicompanionProject>",
  "model": "gemini-3-flash",
  "request": { "contents": [...], "systemInstruction": {...}, "tools": [...], "generationConfig": {...} },
  "userAgent": "antigravity",
  "requestId": "<uuid per request>"
}
```

Differences from the CLI dialect: no `user_prompt_id`, no `session_id`, `requestId` is used for retry de-duplication, and `userAgent` identifies the client.

## Project discovery

`loadCodeAssist` with:

```json
{ "metadata": { "ideType": "ANTIGRAVITY", "platform": "PLATFORM_UNSPECIFIED", "pluginType": "GEMINI" } }
```

The response carries `allowedTiers`, `currentTier`, `paidTier` and `cloudaicompanionProject`. If no project is returned, `onboardUser` is called with the default tier (`cloudaicompanionProject` omitted for `free-tier`), polled until `done`, then `loadCodeAssist` is retried once.

## Model discovery

`POST /v1internal:fetchAvailableModels` with `{ "project": "<id>" }` returns:

```jsonc
{
  "models": {
    "gemini-3-flash": {
      "displayName": "Gemini 3 Flash",
      "maxTokens": 1048576,
      "maxOutputTokens": 65536,
      "supportsImages": true,
      "supportsThinking": true,
      "isInternal": false,
      "quotaInfo": { "remainingFraction": 0.92, "resetTime": "2026-10-31T19:29:46Z" }
    }
  }
}
```

Rules applied by the plugin:

* drop `isInternal: true`, `chat_*` ids, retired ids (`gemini-2.5-pro`, `tab_flash_lite_preview`);
* use `maxTokens` / `maxOutputTokens` as context / output limits;
* the same `quotaInfo` drives the auto-continue reset lookup, so no separate quota call is needed.

Some advertised ids are not actually serviceable. `gemini-3.1-pro-high` returns a detail-less 400; the Hub's working high-effort route is `gemini-pro-agent`, which the fallback catalogue uses. `gemini-3.5-flash-high` maps to `gemini-3-flash-agent`.

## Errors

Same Google RPC envelope as the CLI profile. `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` with `RetryInfo.retryDelay` or a per-model `quotaInfo.resetTime` feeds the same gate described above.

## Confidence

The Antigravity profile is reconstructed from public protocol documentation and independent client implementations, then exercised end to end against OpenCode with a mock backend. A live account is required to validate entitlements and model inventory, because those are account-specific.


## Account limits: `retrieveUserQuotaSummary`

`fetchAvailableModels` only carries a per-model 5-hour fraction. The 5-hour
and weekly limits shown in the Antigravity usage page come from a separate
call:

```http
POST /v1internal:retrieveUserQuotaSummary
{ "project": "<cloudaicompanionProject>" }
```

```jsonc
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "displayName": "Gemini Models",
      "buckets": [
        { "bucketId": "gemini-weekly", "window": "weekly", "remainingFraction": 0.997, "resetTime": "2026-11-07T16:45:50Z" },
        { "bucketId": "gemini-5h",     "window": "5h",     "remainingFraction": 0.990, "resetTime": "2026-10-31T21:45:50Z" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "displayName": "Claude and GPT models",
      "buckets": [
        { "bucketId": "3p-weekly", "window": "weekly", "remainingFraction": 0.990, "resetTime": "2026-11-07T16:46:05Z" },
        { "bucketId": "3p-5h",     "window": "5h",     "remainingFraction": 0.979, "resetTime": "2026-10-31T21:46:05Z" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

There are therefore two pools (Gemini, Claude/GPT), each with a 5-hour and a
weekly window. The plugin keys them as `gemini` and `3p`, shows the active
model's pool in the sidebar, and uses the same data for the auto-continue
reset lookup (falling back to per-model `quotaInfo` if the summary endpoint is
unavailable).
